logical_components.name: ApiRouter
logical_components.description: HTTP entrypoint. Parses requests, dispatches to the store, loads plugins. The application's front door.

logical_components.name: Store
logical_components.description: In-memory + persisted record store. Read and written by multiple callers; the shared-state hub of the service.

logical_components.name: PluginLoader
logical_components.description: Discovers and instantiates external plugins against a typed Protocol. The intended extension seam.

logical_components.name: LegacyExport
logical_components.description: Old CSV export path superseded by the plugin system. Still wired into the router but no longer used by any live caller. STRIP candidate.

edges.evidence: Both router request handlers and the background flush task read/write Store.records without a single-writer contract.
src/router.py:118 — legacy /export route still calls legacy_export.write_csv
legacy_export assumes Store records are already flushed before it reads them; nothing in code, types, or tests enforces that ordering — the invariant lives only in the original author's head.

prune_candidates.latent_bug_fixed: The background-knowledge flush-ordering invariant disappears once legacy-export is gone — no remaining caller depends on it.

core_boundary.rationale: Core is the request/store path every feature needs. The seam is the plugin loader (weakest connascence: Name + Type via the Protocol). Removable is the legacy export, kept alive only by one router route, with a background-knowledge edge to the store that is the architectural prize for pruning.
open_questions: store (today core; could become a seam if persistence is made host-injectable)
